Extreme close-up still life at night. A single branch of old gnarled plum wood with one fully open five-petalled white-and-sage plum blossom (maehwa), petals spread wide and trembling. A small butterfly of hammered gold, delicate openwork wings, has pushed its body deep into the heart of the blossom, wings pressed open, gold legs gripping the petals; a burst of pollen dust spills from the stamens and drifts glowing in the air. Cold ice-blue #7EB8F0 moonlight from above grazes the petals; a warm guttering lamp glow from below catches the gold. Sage green #8AAFA0 in the leaves and the blurred background, crushed black night beyond, a few fallen petals on dark timber below. Delicate, intimate, suggestive. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
